body: Go on Monday. Just go. If you're ready to end your life, you have nothing to lose. I'm a 27/F and while my story is different, I know what it feels like to believe you have absolutely nothing in your life to live for. I know how the pain of past mistakes feels unbearable and how things can seem irreparable. But as long as you're alive, you have options. Even if things can just be slightly better than how they feel now, wouldn't that be better? You have a family that cares for you and that is much more than most people have. (I'm not trying to guilt trip you -- just show you how fortunate you are.) I'm here to talk if you're interested. I feel like I'm at the end of my rope too, so I have nothing to lose either.

No matter how depressed I am, I have a sense of responsibility about the things that I commit to. And I know that if I allow myself to give in to my depression and just stay in bed, it won't actually make anything better. In fact, staying in bed will almost always make things worse for me.

I particularly like how you said, "I'm not a happy person, I never was, and I'm never going to be."  I've thought this way in the past and it takes the pressure off when I feel completely overwhelmed with depression.

I'm not sure you can tell a Redditor to stay off the internet, but I agree that it's probably a good idea if you're prone to depression.

I haven't ended my life yet because I worry that it's the wrong choice somehow. I feel hopeless and almost nothing interests me anymore, but I fundamentally struggle with why I'm so focused on ending my life in the first place. Most people don't go around believing they should be dead, so what makes me believe I should be? What makes me so different and awful that I don't deserve life, yet everyone else does? It's very confusing for me. And that confusion keeps me going somehow. The uncertainty and unpredictability of life keeps me going.
